newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: German state premier talks of EMU delay plan-paper.
newsitem.headline: German state premier talks of EMU delay plan-paper.

text.p: The premier of the German state of Bavaria, Edmund Stoiber, has talked of a plan to delay the launch of European economic and monetary union (EMU) from 1999 to 2001, Dutch newspaper Algemeen Dagblad said on Wednesday.

Algemeen Dagblad described Stoiber -- a member of Finance Minister Theo Waigel's Christian Social Union (CSU) party -- as the "spiritual father" of the plan and said he had talked about it in a 90-minute interview with the paper on Tuesday.
"Waigel knows our situation and anybody who can add up three and three knows that this (plan) is the only alternative for a further prudent development," Stoiber was quoted as saying.

He was also quoted as saying the plan was not yet being debated openly because final 1997 figures were not yet available on European Union member states' compliance with the Maastricht qualification criteria for EMU.
"We don't want to conduct a debate now about a real delay. Furthermore, remarks by the Finance Minister are weighed quite differently," he said.
Stoiber said a two-year delay was permissible under the Maastricht Treaty which sets out the terms for EMU.
Key EU member states Germany and France both face a tough fight to meet EMU budgetary targets this year.
